## Reading, session by session

The papers below are the ones worth reading in full.

### Session 1 — Foundations

- Nathan R, Getz WM, Revilla E, Holyoak M, Kadmon R, Saltz D, Smouse PE (2008).
  *A movement ecology paradigm for unifying organismal movement research.*
  PNAS 105:19052–19059.
  [doi:10.1073/pnas.0800375105](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.0800375105) —
  the spine of the course.
- Kays R, Crofoot MC, Jetz W, Wikelski M (2015). *Terrestrial animal tracking
  as an eye on life and planet.* Science 348:aaa2478.
  [doi:10.1126/science.aaa2478](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaa2478) —
  the opening bookend.
- Hebblewhite M, Haydon DT (2010). *Distinguishing technology from biology: a
  critical review of the use of GPS telemetry data in ecology.* Phil Trans R
  Soc B 365:2303–2312.
  [doi:10.1098/rstb.2010.0087](https://doi.org/10.1098/rstb.2010.0087)
- Laundré JW, Hernández L, Altendorf KB (2001). *Wolves, elk, and bison:
  reestablishing the "landscape of fear" in Yellowstone National Park, U.S.A.*
  Canadian Journal of Zoology 79:1401–1409.
- Portugal SJ, White CR (2018). *Miniaturization of biologgers is not
  alleviating the 5% rule.* Methods Ecol Evol 9:1662–1666.
  [doi:10.1111/2041-210X.13013](https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.13013)
- Laube P, Purves RS (2011). *How fast is a cow? Cross-scale analysis of
  movement data.* Transactions in GIS 15:401–418 — the sampling-interval
  problem, quantified.

### Session 2 — Spatial data in R

- **[Geocomputation with R](https://r.geocompx.org/)** — Lovelace, Nowosad,
  Muenchow. Free, excellent, the default recommendation.
- **[Spatial Data Science with applications in R](https://r-spatial.org/book/)** —
  Pebesma & Bivand, by the author of `sf`.
- **[rspatial.org](https://rspatial.org/)** — Hijmans, the `terra` reference.
- Pettorelli N, Vik JO, Mysterud A, Gaillard J-M, Tucker CJ, Stenseth NC (2005).
  *Using the satellite-derived NDVI to assess ecological responses to
  environmental change.* TREE 20:503–510.
  [doi:10.1016/j.tree.2005.05.011](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tree.2005.05.011)
- Data portals: [Copernicus Browser](https://browser.dataspace.copernicus.eu/)
  (Sentinel), [USGS EarthExplorer](https://earthexplorer.usgs.gov/) (Landsat),
  [NASA AppEEARS](https://appeears.earthdatacloud.nasa.gov/),
  [Movebank Env-DATA](https://www.movebank.org/cms/movebank-content/env-data).

### Session 3 — From fixes to trajectories

- Calenge C (2006). *The package "adehabitat" for the R software: a tool for
  the analysis of space and habitat use by animals.* Ecological Modelling
  197:516–519.
- Signer J, Fieberg J, Avgar T (2019). *Animal movement tools (`amt`): R
  package for managing tracking data and conducting habitat selection
  analyses.* Ecol Evol 9:880–890.
  [doi:10.1002/ece3.4823](https://doi.org/10.1002/ece3.4823)

### Session 4 — Quantifying movement

- Benhamou S (2004). *How to reliably estimate the tortuosity of an animal's
  path: straightness, sinuosity, or fractal dimension?* J Theor Biol
  229:209–220.
- Turchin P (1996). *Fractal analyses of animal movement: a critique.* Ecology
  77:2086–2090.
- Fauchald P, Tveraa T (2003). *Using first-passage time in the analysis of
  area-restricted search and habitat selection.* Ecology 84:282–288.
- Bunnefeld N, Börger L, van Moorter B, Rolandsen CM, Dettki H, Solberg EJ,
  Ericsson G (2011). *A model-driven approach to quantify migration patterns:
  individual, regional and yearly differences.* J Anim Ecol 80:466–476.
- Gurarie E, Andrews RD, Laidre KL (2009). *A novel method for identifying
  behavioural changes in animal movement data.* Ecology Letters 12:395–408 —
  behavioural change-point analysis (`bcpa`).
- Edelhoff H, Signer J, Balkenhol N (2016). *Path segmentation for beginners:
  an overview of current methods for detecting changes in animal movement
  patterns.* Movement Ecology 4:21.

### Session 5 — Movement models and simulation

- Codling EA, Plank MJ, Benhamou S (2008). *Random walk models in biology.*
  J R Soc Interface 5:813–834.
  [doi:10.1098/rsif.2008.0014](https://doi.org/10.1098/rsif.2008.0014)
- Viswanathan GM, Afanasyev V, Buldyrev SV, Murphy EJ, Prince PA, Stanley HE
  (1996). *Lévy flight search patterns of wandering albatrosses.* Nature
  381:413–415.
- Edwards AM et al. (2007). *Revisiting Lévy flight search patterns of
  wandering albatrosses, bumblebees and deer.* Nature 449:1044–1048.
- Benhamou S (2007). *How many animals really do the Lévy walk?* Ecology
  88:1962–1969.
- Clauset A, Shalizi CR, Newman MEJ (2009). *Power-law distributions in
  empirical data.* SIAM Review 51:661–703 — how to fit a power law properly.
- Humphries NE et al. (2010). *Environmental context explains Lévy and
  Brownian movement patterns of marine predators.* Nature 465:1066–1069.

### Session 6 — Home ranges

- Powell RA, Mitchell MS (2012). *What is a home range?* J Mammal 93:948–958.
  [doi:10.1644/11-MAMM-S-177.1](https://doi.org/10.1644/11-MAMM-S-177.1)
- Worton BJ (1989). *Kernel methods for estimating the utilization distribution
  in home-range studies.* Ecology 70:164–168.
- Horne JS, Garton EO, Krone SM, Lewis JS (2007). *Analyzing animal movements
  using Brownian bridges.* Ecology 88:2354–2363.
- Fleming CH, Fagan WF, Mueller T, Olson KA, Leimgruber P, Calabrese JM (2015).
  *Rigorous home range estimation with movement data: a new autocorrelated
  kernel density estimator.* Ecology 96:1182–1188.
  [doi:10.1890/14-2010.1](https://doi.org/10.1890/14-2010.1)
- Calabrese JM, Fleming CH, Gurarie E (2016). *ctmm: an R package for analyzing
  animal relocation data as a continuous-time stochastic process.* Methods Ecol
  Evol 7:1124–1132.
- Börger L, Dalziel BD, Fryxell JM (2008). *Are there general mechanisms of
  animal home range behaviour? A review and prospects for future research.*
  Ecology Letters 11:637–650.

### Session 7 — Habitat selection

- Fortin D, Beyer HL, Boyce MS, Smith DW, Duchesne T, Mao JS (2005). *Wolves
  influence elk movements: behavior shapes a trophic cascade in Yellowstone
  National Park.* Ecology 86:1320–1330 — the step selection function.
- Lele SR, Keim JL (2006). *Weighted distributions and estimation of resource
  selection probability functions.* Ecology 87:3021–3028.
- Avgar T, Potts JR, Lewis MA, Boyce MS (2016). *Integrated step selection
  analysis: bridging the gap between resource selection and animal movement.*
  Methods Ecol Evol 7:619–630.
  [doi:10.1111/2041-210X.12528](https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.12528)
- Avgar T, Lele SR, Keim JL, Boyce MS (2017). *Relative selection strength:
  quantifying effect size in habitat- and step-selection inference.* Ecol Evol
  7:5322–5330.
- Fieberg J, Signer J, Smith B, Avgar T (2021). *A "how-to" guide for
  interpreting parameters in habitat-selection analyses.* J Anim Ecol
  90:1027–1043.
  [doi:10.1111/1365-2656.13441](https://doi.org/10.1111/1365-2656.13441) —
  **the single most useful paper in this course.**
- Muff S, Signer J, Fieberg J (2020). *Accounting for individual-specific
  variation in habitat-selection studies.* J Anim Ecol 89:80–92.
- LaPoint S, Gallery P, Wikelski M, Kays R (2013). *Animal behavior, cost-based
  corridor models, and real corridors.* Landscape Ecology 28:1615–1630 — the
  fisher data.

### Session 8 — Hidden Markov models and the frontier

- Langrock R, King R, Matthiopoulos J, Thomas L, Fortin D, Morales JM (2012).
  *Flexible and practical modeling of animal telemetry data: hidden Markov
  models and extensions.* Ecology 93:2336–2342.
- McClintock BT, Michelot T (2018). *momentuHMM: R package for generalized
  hidden Markov models of animal movement.* Methods Ecol Evol 9:1518–1530.
- McClintock BT, Langrock R, Gimenez O, Cam E, Borchers DL, Glennie R,
  Patterson TA (2020). *Uncovering ecological state dynamics with hidden Markov
  models.* Ecology Letters 23:1878–1903 — the review to read.
- Jonsen ID, Mills Flemming J, Myers RA (2005). *Robust state–space modeling of
  animal movement data.* Ecology 86:2874–2880.
- Johnson DS, London JM, Lea M-A, Durban JW (2008). *Continuous-time correlated
  random walk model for animal telemetry data.* Ecology 89:1208–1215.
- Wilson RP, Quintana F, Hobson VJ (2012). *Construction of energy landscapes
  can clarify the movement and distribution of foraging animals.* Proc R Soc B
  279:975–980; and Shepard ELC et al. (2013). *Energy landscapes shape animal
  movement ecology.* Am Nat 182:298–312.
- Couzin ID, Krause J, Franks NR, Levin SA (2005). *Effective leadership and
  decision-making in animal groups on the move.* Nature 433:513–516.
- Nathan R, Spiegel O, Fortmann-Roe S, Harel R, Wikelski M, Getz WM (2012).
  *Using tri-axial acceleration data to identify behavioral modes of
  free-ranging animals.* J Exp Biol 215:986–996.
- Wang G (2019). *Machine learning for inferring animal behavior from location
  and movement data.* Ecological Informatics 49:69–76.
- Nathan R et al. (2022). *Big-data approaches lead to an increased
  understanding of the ecology of animal movement.* Science 375:eabg1780 — the
  closing bookend.

## Books

- Hooten MB, Johnson DS, McClintock BT, Morales JM (2017).
  *Animal Movement: Statistical Models for Telemetry Data.* CRC Press.
  The rigorous reference. Heavy on maths, worth it.
- Fieberg J (2024). *[Statistics for Ecologists: A Frequentist and Bayesian
  Treatment of Modern Regression Models](https://statistics4ecologists-v3.netlify.app/)*
  — free online, with excellent habitat-selection chapters.
- Cagnacci F, Boitani L, Powell RA, Boyce MS, eds. (2010). Special issue on
  GPS telemetry, Phil Trans R Soc B 365(1550) — still the best single
  collection of overviews.

## Software and communities

| | |
|:--|:--|
| [`amt`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=amt) | Tracks, steps, resampling, RSF/SSF — used in most sessions |
| [`adehabitatLT`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=adehabitatLT) | Trajectories (`ltraj`), NSD, first-passage time |
| [`bcpa`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=bcpa) | Behavioural change-point analysis |
| [`move2`](https://bartk.gitlab.io/move2/) | Movebank access and the modern `move` successor |
| [`ctmm`](https://ctmm-initiative.github.io/ctmm/) | Continuous-time models, AKDE. Has a [point-and-click app](https://ctmm.shinyapps.io/ctmmweb/). |
| [`momentuHMM`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=momentuHMM) | Hidden Markov models with covariates and multiple data streams |
| [`adehabitatHR`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=adehabitatHR) | Classic home range estimators |
| [`sf`](https://r-spatial.github.io/sf/) / [`terra`](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/) | The spatial foundation |
| [AniMove](https://animove.org/) | Annual summer school — the best training available in this field |
| [Movebank](https://www.movebank.org/) | Data repository; also hosts Env-DATA annotation |

## Getting help

When code breaks, in this order:

1. **Read the error message.** Genuinely. Most R errors name the object and the
   function that failed.
2. `?function_name` and the package **vignettes**
   (`browseVignettes("amt")`) — these are written by the people who wrote the
   code.
3. [r-spatial on Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/r+sf)
   and the [`amt` GitHub issues](https://github.com/jmsigner/amt/issues).
4. Ask me — but bring a **reproducible example**: the smallest piece of code
   plus the smallest piece of data that reproduces the problem. Building that
   example solves the problem about half the time by itself.
